items.evidence: The AC#1 test passes and asserts the exact [fold, call] list for seats 1, 2 and 3 (16/14/12), illegal-action on the raise, and the 3-bet control. Mutants that remove or loosen the cap fail it. Holdout: the same script, extended through seats 4 (call 8) and 5 (call 4), gives exact [fold, call] each time. Raises to +1 unit, +2 units and the current bet, plus a bet, are all rejected, and the input state is deep-equal afterwards. The street then closes to the flop with betCount 0 and a bet offered.

Recorded deviation verified on substance. On a 3-seat flop (seat 2 bets 4, seat 3 to 8, seat 1 to 12, seat 2 to 16), seat 3 has 8 in and owes 8. On the turn and river (8/16/24/32), seat 3 has 16 in and owes 16. No seat owes 12 or 24, so the spec's literal 12/24 is arithmetically impossible, and the test's 8/16/16 matches the §5 worked example (turn call 16). Holdout: one hand plays a capped flop, turn and river in sequence. Each street resets betCount to 0, offers a raise at 3 bets, and gives exact [fold, call] at 4 (seat 3 then seat 1). Higher raises are rejected illegal-action.

The AC#3 test passes. Holdout: heads-up blinds are seat 1 $2 and seat 2 $4. After 8/12/16, seat 2 gets exactly [fold, call 4]. On the flop after limp and check, bet 4 and raises to 8/12/16 leave the first player with [fold, call 4]. After a limp the BB still has the raise option (betCount 1).

The AC#4 test passes inside the full suite (100,000 hands, 0 violations, non-vacuous). Holdout: 18,000 runPlaytest hands with randomMovePolicy at sizes 2-10 and different seeds (9000+size) had 0 streets over 4 records, more than 0 streets at exactly 4, and 0 violations. An aggressive random walk (5,400 hands, varied stacks 20-219, sizes 2-10) checked every decision. Raise/bet was never offered at betCount 4 and a raise was always rejected there. A raise was always offered below the cap when currentBet > 0 and affordable. checkState was clean throughout and records per street stayed at 4 or fewer. The same holdout run against the pre-change engine fails thousands of these checks, so it discriminates.

The AC#6 'fifth raise' test passes and asserts the full rejection object. Holdout: STREET_BET_CAP === 4. At every capped spot there is no raise or bet in legalActions, applyAction of raise or bet returns ok:false illegal-action, and the state is not mutated. A short stack at the cap gets [fold, call min(owed, stack)] (call 6 with 6 left).

The AC#5 test passes. Holdout: AsAh on seat 1 at 4 bets gives a view with no raise, recommendPreflop.action 'call' and an alternative that is not 'raise'. A synthetic view that wrongly includes a raise at betCount 4 is still advised 'call', which shows the advice cap clause works on its own. At 3 bets the same hand is advised 'raise'. preflop.ts has no local CAP and uses STREET_BET_CAP. Note: the builder test kills the 'advice clause removed' mutant only through its source-text check, but the holdout confirms the behaviour.

The AC#6 checker test and the invariants unit test pass. The locked TASK-1.8 invariants acceptance test passes unchanged with the A-4 fixture. Holdout: FAULTS.fifthBet at size 6 seed 42 over 20 hands gives bet-cap >= 1, all others 0, and the message matches '<street> has 5 bets (at most 4)'. Sizes 2, 3 and 10 (50 hands, seed 7) are also bet-cap only. A state forged from a real 4-bet preflop plus a fifth raise record, with betCount 3, is flagged bet-cap by checkState. invariants.ts has no STREET_BET_CAP and keeps MAX_BETS_PER_STREET = 4.

The policy unit test passes, and the re-filter mutant fails it. Holdout: on a synthetic capped view that includes a raise, randomMovePolicy draws fold, call and raise over 300 seeds. On the real capped view it draws only {call, fold}. An empty legal set throws RangeError. policy.ts contains no 'betCount'.
